sections.section: 2.3.1. Normalizing Aortic Root and Ascending Aortic Diameters for Body Size
content: Acknowledges the challenge of defining normal aortic size in children due to the variability in body size.
Recommends using methods such as the Z-score to assess aortic dilation in children.
Discusses normalizing aortic diameter using clinical and research practices.

subsections.name: The Z-Score
content: Z-score is used to assess aortic dilation in the pediatric population.
Discusses the limitations of BSA for calculating the Z-score.
Indicates limited literature on acute aortic syndromes (AAS) using Z-scores.

subsections.name: The Aortic Size Index and Aortic Height Index
content: Aortic diameters normalized using ratios like the Aortic Size Index (ASI) and Aortic Height Index (AHI).
Mention of better prediction of adverse events using ASI.
Zafar et al. found AHI may perform better than ASI for predicting aortic growth.

subsections.name: The Cross-Sectional Area to Height Ratio
content: Alternative method proposed by Svensson et al. in 2002 for normalizing aortic size to height.
